summary: Hosted API: customer-reported availability (~98.8%) does not match Redwood SLO dashboard (~99.96%) for streaming chat; suspected 499/timeout attribution
description:
Customer (HelioCRM) reports a mismatch between their measured availability for streaming chat completions and Redwood Console SLO dashboard.

Issue summary
- HelioCRM observes ~98.8–99.1% “successful requests” from their client telemetry for /v1/chat/completions (stream=true).
- Redwood Console → Reliability → Hosted API SLO shows ~99.96% availability for the same window.
- Customer believes Redwood is undercounting failures by excluding timeouts / disconnects.

Impact
- Customer escalation: they need accurate availability reporting for internal SLO/SLA reporting and post-incident review.
- Risk: misalignment on what Redwood counts as an error for Hosted tier; potential trust issue.

Time window
- 2026-02-11 18:00–23:30 UTC (highest discrepancy)
- Customer also notes intermittent recurrence on 2026-02-10.

Environment
- Hosted API, prod, region us-east
- Models: rw-llama-70b-instruct (primary), rw-mixtral-8x22b (fallback)

Customer evidence (from HelioCRM)
- Their logs show spikes of HTTP 499 and client-side timeouts around 60s.
- Representative request IDs provided by customer:
  - x-request-id: hcrm_01HSZ6J1G9K8F8 (HTTP 499)
  - x-request-id: hcrm_01HSZ6M2Q2V0B1 (client timeout; no final status captured)
- They consider these “Redwood failures” because requests stall or streams terminate unexpectedly.

Redwood observed
- SLO dashboard panel shows low 5xx but elevated 499s during the same window.
- Current Hosted availability SLI query excludes 499 by default as “client abort” per earlier gateway taxonomy.

Question / ask
- Confirm whether Redwood SLO dashboard should exclude 499 for streaming endpoints.
- If exclusions are correct, provide a written definition HelioCRM can adopt.
- If exclusions are incorrect, fix SLI and backfill affected windows.
comments: 2026-02-12 09:14 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support): Opened on behalf of HelioCRM escalation. Customer is comparing their Datadog success-rate vs our Hosted SLO widget. They are counting 499 + client timeouts as failures. Requesting SRE to confirm SLI definition and whether 499 exclusion is intended for streaming.

2026-02-12 10:02 UTC — HelioCRM (Customer, via Support): We saw ~1.2% of calls fail between 18:00–23:30 UTC yesterday. These are primarily 499s and “socket hang up” while waiting for the stream. Your dashboard shows everything is fine (99.9%+). We need the dashboard to reflect what users experienced, otherwise it’s not actionable.

2026-02-12 10:25 UTC — Aisha Bello (SRE): Acknowledged. We currently classify 499 as client abort in the gateway metrics and exclude those from Hosted availability SLI by default. For streaming, we should not blindly exclude 499 because many are caused by upstream stall/timeout rather than user cancel. Pulling gateway + routing traces for the specific window; will report back with a proposed correction and a written definition for HelioCRM.

2026-02-12 11:10 UTC — Nadia Rahman (Observability): Confirming metrics pipeline behavior: in api-gateway, 499 increments http_requests_total{status="499",disconnect_class="client_abort"} for any request closed by client before completion. This is overbroad for streaming because we cannot currently distinguish a user-initiated cancel from client timeout triggered by slow TTFT / stalled stream.

2026-02-12 12:03 UTC — Amara Diallo (API Gateway): We shipped the first pass of streaming disconnect classification recently (client_abort vs server_disconnect) but 499 mapping is still too coarse. For the timeframe in question, many 499s correspond to gateway timing out waiting for upstream headers (should have been 504/5xx class) vs true user cancellation.

2026-02-12 13:22 UTC — Aisha Bello (SRE): Initial finding: a non-trivial subset of 499s in this window are actually gateway-enforced upstream timeouts (client sees close, gateway emits 499). This makes the SLO query look “better” than the customer experience if we exclude all 499. Proposed change: treat 499 with upstream_timeout=true (or derived from gateway timeout reason) as server-fault for availability SLI; only exclude 499 when we have positive signal of user cancellation.

2026-02-12 14:05 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support): Relayed to customer that we likely have an attribution bug in our SLI (not just a definition disagreement). Customer asked for an ETA and whether dashboards will be corrected retroactively.

2026-02-13 09:18 UTC — Aisha Bello (SRE): Created hotfix PR to correct miscounting of 499/timeout errors in Hosted availability SLI and update SLO toolkit query examples. Will also update the Confluence SLI spec to explicitly state which client-side timeouts are excluded vs which gateway timeouts are included as server faults.

2026-02-13 17:40 UTC — Sergio Costa (Dashboards): Once PR lands, we can backfill the affected window(s) in the SLO job and the dashboard should align more closely with customer-observed availability. Expect delta mainly in streaming availability for us-east during the incident window.

2026-02-14 08:32 UTC — HelioCRM (Customer, via Support): Thanks. Please confirm the final definition we should use: If a stream terminates because the client hits its timeout waiting for tokens, do you count it as a failure? In our case, users didn’t cancel, they waited and the stream closed.

2026-02-14 09:05 UTC — Aisha Bello (SRE): Definition clarification draft for Hosted tier (streaming):
1) User-initiated cancels (explicit client cancel) are excluded.
2) Client timeouts caused by customer-configured short deadlines are excluded only when we have no evidence Redwood stalled (no upstream timeout / no server-side disconnect).
3) Gateway-enforced upstream timeouts and server-side disconnects are included as failures.
We are tightening our instrumentation so we can distinguish (1) vs (3) for 499-like outcomes. Will provide final written language after the PR merges and dashboards confirm alignment.

2026-02-18 16:12 UTC — Aisha Bello (SRE): Hotfix merged and deployed. Hosted availability SLI now counts gateway upstream timeouts correctly (no longer excluded under generic 499 bucket). Backfill run completed for 2026-02-10 through 2026-02-14. Console SLO for the reported window in us-east now shows 99.05% availability, which matches HelioCRM’s observed 98.8–99.1% range given slight differences in sampling and retries.
2026-02-18 16:20 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support): Shared updated dashboard numbers + definition summary with customer. Asked them to validate against their telemetry for the same UTC window.

2026-02-19 07:55 UTC — HelioCRM (Customer, via Support): We re-ran our report and the numbers are now consistent with your dashboard (within ~0.1%). The written definition also helps. Please keep us posted if there are future changes to streaming SLO measurement.

2026-02-21 10:11 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support): Closing ticket per customer confirmation. Internal follow-up: ensure SLI spec + tiered SLO page reference the corrected 499/timeout handling and that future changes go through the SLO review process.
resolution: Resolved by metrics/SLI attribution hotfix: gateway upstream timeouts that previously surfaced as 499 and were excluded from Hosted availability are now counted as server-side failures for streaming availability SLI. Backfilled SLO calculations for the affected dates; Console dashboards updated and now align with customer-observed availability. Provided customer-facing SLI definition/exclusions for streaming cancels vs timeouts.
root_cause: SLI definition + instrumentation mismatch for streaming endpoints: HTTP 499 was treated as “client abort” and excluded from availability, but a subset of 499s were caused by gateway/upstream timeouts (server-fault) during an incident window, resulting in inflated availability in Redwood dashboards.
next_steps: 1) Update and socialize SLI spec for streaming disconnects/timeouts (owner: Aisha Bello / Nadia Rahman). 2) Ensure api-gateway emits explicit timeout reason labels to reduce ambiguity between user cancel and server timeout (owner: Amara Diallo). 3) Add regression test in slo-toolkit for 499/timeout classification (owner: Nadia Rahman). 4) Include this case study in SLO program rollout notes to avoid future customer confusion (owner: Elliot Price).
